data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A diagnostic test is a passive measurement of a fixed biological state, while a checklist is an active procedural intervention executed by human agents subject to interpretation and aggregation effects.","The Condorcet/aggregation layer of the panel has no direct equivalent in a single diagnostic test's false positive rate.","Diagnostic test accuracy is usually validated across multiple populations, whereas the claim concerns a single evaluation."],"overturn_conditions":["Discovery that checklist compliance somehow yields correct answers on structurally adversarial items without the checklist encoding causal structure (e.g., via latent panel-member reasoning overriding the checklist).","Evidence that domain experts also fail the adversarial items at equal or higher rates, suggesting the items test something other than structure-vs-surface."],"shared_structure":["Both a checklist and a diagnostic medical test encode a 'frozen theory' mapping observable inputs to a predicted outcome.","Both can be followed mechanically (compliance) without understanding the underlying causal mechanism.","Both face adversarial conditions: for tests, a confounding disease mimicking the target biomarker; for checklists, an item where checklist-cued features diverge from causal determinants of the outcome."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a diagnostic test's false positive rate spikes on confounders, a checklist's 'reliability' will collapse on adversarial items if it only encodes surface correlations.","Just as a test that tracks causal pathways remains robust to confounders, a checklist capturing genuine structure will maintain performance on adversarial items."]},"claim":"A single evaluation can distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance if and only if it contains adversarial items where checklist-indicated cues and the underlying causal structure diverge; under those items, mere compliance will fail while genuine reliability (understanding the structure) will hold.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The evaluation distribution contains no adversarial items where surface cues and structural causes diverge, making compliance and genuine reasoning indistinguishable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist author intended it as a purely surface-level heuristic with no claim to causal structure, rendering the compliance-vs-genuine distinction moot.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The single evaluation is conducted on a narrow distribution where the checklist's surface correlations happen to perfectly align with causal structure, preventing any internal distinction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A checklist encodes a theory as observable cues. If the checklist captures genuine causal structure, following it yields correct answers even on adversarial items (where surface cues are misleading but the checklist's structural cues remain valid). If it merely tracks surface correlations, adversarial items that break those correlations will cause checklist-compliant answers to fail. Thus, within a single evaluation, the delta between performance on standard items and adversarial items isolates the 'frozen theory quality' component, separating it from rote compliance.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
